summary: In this tafseer session on Surat Al-Anbiya, Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains the opening descriptions of the Quran as a "remembrance" (dhikr) and "blessed" (mubarak). The Quran is described as a remembrance because it reconnects people with their natural disposition (fitra) of worshipping Allah alone, as they are born with this innate knowledge. The term "blessed" refers to the abundance of enduring good that Allah has sent down. Sh. Ali Mashhour then introduces the upcoming prophets' stories in the chapter (Ibrahim, Lut, Nuh, Dawood, Suleiman, Ayyub, Zakariya, and Yahya), explaining that while all prophets came with the complete message, each prophet's story emphasizes different aspects of prophethood—such as Ibrahim's emphasis on tawhid, Nuh's deliverance, and Lut's stance against sexual perversion.
